changes.ut-good-faith: L212-1 defines unfairness by significant imbalance without making proof of a separate good-faith breach a prerequisite. This can provide wider protection under EU Article 8; no gap inferred from omitted words.
changes.ut-conclusion: L212-1 expressly assesses circumstances existing at contract conclusion and all linked terms and contracts.
changes.ut-renewal: L215-1 provides dedicated advance notice before the objection period ends, free termination and refunds if notice omitted. L212-1 general unfairness also covers other terms and contracts; service-law sectoral exceptions do not themselves prove an unfairness exemption.
changes.ut-seller-definition: Current preliminary article, points 1–3: natural-person consumer outside profession; professional includes natural/legal, public/private persons, acting for another professional.
changes.ut-price-scope: L212-1 excludes main subject and adequacy of price or remuneration relative to the sold good/service only where clear and comprehensible. It does not exempt every price term.
changes.ut-mandatory-terms: No free-standing broad exemption for seller-created terms in current L212-1. EU Article 1(2) exception is not a duty to reduce stronger national protection. Specific mandatory sectoral rules not exhaustively certified.
changes.ut-binding-contract: L241-1: unfair terms deemed unwritten; rest of contract survives if capable; rule is mandatory public policy.
changes.ut-prevention: Current L621-7 and L621-8 permit collective injunctions and removal from proposed, intended and existing contracts, declaration unwritten in identical contracts and notice to consumers. L524-1–2 provide public-authority court routes; R632-1 requires ex officio exclusion after hearing parties.
changes.ut-sole-will: R212-2(1) expressly covers professional performance depending on its sole will; mandatory general L212-1 applies.
changes.ut-price-date: R212-1(3) prohibits unilateral price change in blacklisted scope, with defined R212-3–4 financial and indefinite-contract qualifications; general imbalance review remains. No requirement to copy each indicative Annex phrase.
changes.ut-insurance: The corrected recital is interpretive, not an independent new prohibition or requirement to exclude insurer liability. No broad insurance exemption established in L212-1; separate insurance procedures not certified.
changes.ut-interest-received: R212-4 first paragraph expressly covers interest owed by AND owed to the consumer, valid reason, prompt information and immediate termination. Whole R212-3–4 exceptions actually read.
changes.ut-terminology: L212-1 and R212-1–5 use clauses abusives with the operative imbalance test. Word differences alone not treated as a breach.
changes.ut-cz-reprint: Original definitions, negotiation scope, proof, transparency, survival, prevention and conflict law assessed against preliminary article, L212-1, L211-1, L241-1, L232-1, L621-7–8, L524-1–2 and R632-1. All 17 indicative Annex examples considered: a R212-1(6); b (5)–(7); c R212-2(1); d (2); e (3); f R212-1(7)–(9)/R212-2(4); g R212-2(4); h L215-1 plus L212-1; i R212-1(1); j (3)/R212-2(6); k R212-1(3); l same plus general imbalance; m (4); n (2); o (5); p R212-2(5); q R212-1(12)/R212-2(9)–(10). L212-1 covers negotiated and unnegotiated terms, and grey-list proof falls on the professional. L211-1 clarity and consumer-favourable interpretation exclude L621-8 collective proceedings.
changes.ut-notifications: Actual Article 8 a Commission notification performance not verified; no inference from silence in the domestic code.
changes.ut-penalties-general: L241-2 administrative sanctions concern irrebuttably blacklisted terms; L241-1-1 civil fine concerns continued use after final judgment. These are expressly permitted EU Article 8 b(2) options. General effectiveness in every outcome not certified.
changes.ut-penalty-factors: Current L522-1–10 administrative procedure actually read, including reasoned decision and cumulative sanctions. No express complete six-factor Article 8 b(3) route located in these bodies; wider constitutional/judicial and administrative guidance routes remain unclosed. Partial-review blocker, not proof of omission.
changes.ut-wide-penalties: L241-2 and L241-1-1 allow 4% of average of last three known annual turnovers and EUR2m when data unavailable, for CPC widespread infringements following a mutual-assistance request under L511-10. L511-10 includes requests by another Member State OR the Commission. Whether every required Article21 coordinated-action scenario is reached, and the turnover basis, require interpretation. No uncovered cohort established; HOLD public. Independent EU-side challenge: coordinated action by agreement need not use separate mutual assistance (CPC17(1),19(2),21); national equivalence remains open. EU text specifies no particular turnover reference year, so a three-year average is not treated as a demonstrated breach.
changes.ut-penalty-notification: L241-2 current note confirms 28 May2022 application; L241-1-1 later amended3May2025. Actual EU notification dates and performance unverified.

countryChecks.independentReview: Reference agent independently read authentic CPC Regulation Articles17,19,21. Coordinated action may begin by agreement under17(1), with mutual assistance optional under19(2); Art21 imposes enforcement duties without universally requiring a separate request. This supports retaining the precise French request-trigger qualification, not a breach conclusion. National French bodies were read by root only. Reference withdrew a claimed preceding-financial-year rule: EU Art8b4 specifies annual turnover but no reference year; nonbinding Commission2021 parallel Omnibus guidance likewise says the year is undefined. No three-year-average breach inferred.
countryChecks.adverseReview: Root read official CCA2021 report sections41–46 and51: administrative punitive sanctions already subject to constitutional proportionality; indicative factors and coordinated actions discussed, with optional legislative precision proposed. This is earlier institutional discussion, not proof that the exact present request-trigger question has been recognised. Report predates current increased maxima and civil-fine reform; cannot support an ongoing omission from old monetary limits. General binding proportionality may supply part of the criteria route, but full six-factor reach remains unclosed. Root also read the entire official2021 ordinance report: Article8 explanation expressly describes the civil fine as following mutual assistance, but describes the administrative4%route more generally as cross-border cooperation. This supports an interpretation question rather than a categorical national gap; the report does not close the full binding six-factor route. Commission implementation-study section1.1.1.11 includes France among countries adopting the criteria to a greater or lesser degree; it does not identify a complete French binding route for each criterion. This is adverse context against claiming omission, while the source-level blocker remains.

changes.ut-good-faith: Article 82(1): terms contrary to good faith causing significant imbalance are unfair; mandatory classification.
changes.ut-conclusion: Article 82(3) expressly assesses circumstances at contract conclusion, not later performance.
changes.ut-renewal: Article 85(2) prohibits automatic fixed-term renewal where the deadline does not effectively allow objection; broader general unfairness remains in Article 82.
changes.ut-seller-definition: Articles 2–4 cover natural and legal traders, public and private, acting directly or through another person.
changes.ut-price-scope: Articles 80, 82–83 and 85 do not reproduce a blanket main-subject or price-adequacy exclusion; stronger review is permitted by Directive Article 8. Current court interpretation not certified.
changes.ut-mandatory-terms: Law 7/1998 Article 4 actually read: international convention terms and generally applicable mandatory statutory/administrative rules excluded; no broader seller-created exclusion established. Consumer-code Article 59 preserves sectoral minimum protection.
changes.ut-binding-contract: Article 83 makes unfair terms void and unwritten while preserving the contract if it can subsist; transparency nullity also applies.
changes.ut-prevention: Articles 53–54 permit injunctions against continued or imminently repeated conduct, including recommendations of unfair terms; public bodies, consumer organisations, prosecutor and eligible foreign bodies have standing.
changes.ut-sole-will: Article 85(7) expressly covers performance dependent solely on the trader’s will.
changes.ut-price-date: Article 85(10) compares final price to the price initially agreed, with objective-reason/termination and lawful index safeguards.
changes.ut-insurance: No separate exclusion of all insurance liability found in Articles 80–91. This corrected EU recital does not itself impose a new freestanding national prohibition.
changes.ut-interest-received: Article 85(3) expressly includes interest owed by the consumer OR to the consumer, lawful index or valid reason, prompt notice and immediate penalty-free termination.
changes.ut-terminology: Articles 82–91 use unfair-term terminology with the correct operative good-faith/imbalance test; no word-copy requirement inferred.
changes.ut-cz-reprint: Articles 3–4, 80, 82–83, 85–91, 53–54 and 67 read, including burden, transparency, all blacklist groups, survival, collective remedies and conflict-law protection. Law 7/1998 cross-reference remains to close. Law 7/1998 Articles 4, 8, 12, 16 and 19 now read; exclusion, nullity and collective injunction routes assessed.
changes.ut-notifications: Actual Commission notification performance is outside this formal national-law assessment; domestic higher protection considered, not treated as an automatic violation.
changes.ut-penalties-general: Articles 47(j), 48 and 49 sanction introduction/existence of unfair terms and failure to remove their effects; benefits, culpability, deterrence and proportionality addressed.
changes.ut-penalty-factors: Articles 48(3)–(5), 49(2)–(3) cover nature, culpability, duration, consumer harm, corrective action, recidivism, benefit, cross-border sanctions and economic capacity.
changes.ut-wide-penalties: Article 49(5) confines the CPC 4%/EUR 2 m maximum to very serious offences, while Article 48(2)(b) initially grades abusive-term offences as serious. Full adverse review considered mandatory upgrades, illicit-benefit multiples, regional-law floors and central CPC competence. No defensible uncovered cohort or binding interpretation established; legal result inconclusive, no public case.
changes.ut-penalty-notification: 2021 national reform applied 28 May 2022, as current article notes confirm. Actual Commission notification is not inferred from national text.

acts.inventoryStatus: Complete original 1991 provisions and annexes, 2008/51 and 2017/853 amending bodies, and 2021/555 operative Articles 1–28 plus Annexes I–IV read. All 12 direct corrigenda and 17 recursive corrigenda reviewed in authentic languages. Three 1991 R 01 legacy HTML tables recovered from official PDF/A 1 b editions: DE/IT B 5 AND→OR, EL can→cannot. changeInventory.change: Expanded firearm and convertibility definitions; essential components include upper and lower receivers. Covers ammunition, dealers, brokers, illicit manufacturing, trafficking and tracing, including inherited translation corrections. Polish combustible-propellant and essential-component terms, Hungarian round-versus-magazine terms, Finnish alternatives and Romanian receiver terminology are included.

changeInventory.change: Alternative official proof of residence; a non-transferable firearms pass valid for at most five years, with weapon, loss and other updates. The ten-year category D exception in the original 1991 text was removed by 2008/51 Article 1(1)(e), then retained as removed in 2017 and 2021. Includes the Hungarian correction requiring lawful acquisition AND holding.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Remove the blanket collector and museum exclusion; retain specified armed-forces, police, public-authority and defence-transfer exclusions. Stricter national protection remains subject to traveller rights. Rights attach to residence, not nationality.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Clear unique marking and registration for firearms manufactured or imported on or after 14 September 2018 and placed on the market; essential-component marking, historical and small-component options, ammunition-package marks and a government-to-civilian transfer mark.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Registration, licensing or authorisation, and integrity and ability checks for both dealers and brokers. For a legal person, checks cover the entity and the natural persons directing it.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Computerised records identify each firearm and its essential components, conversions and ownership. Retention extends 30 years after destruction, with ten-year licensing/customs access and thirty-year criminal-law access, plus purpose-based deletion rules. Earlier 2008 requirements and their 31 December 2014 deadline are followed.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Dealers and brokers record all firearms received or disposed of and hand records over on closure. Electronic reporting must occur without undue delay, with immediate authority updates and continuous ownership links. Includes the Finnish 2008 correction on all firearms and receiver data.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Licence or specific national permission for category C, good cause, age eighteen and no-danger conditions. Supervised youth hunting and target-shooting exceptions concern acquisition other than purchase. Includes Lithuanian and Hungarian corrections on those distinctions.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Monitor continuing authorisation conditions, including relevant medical and psychological information; withdraw permissions when conditions cease. Large centre-fire magazines can require category B withdrawal unless an applicable authorisation or grandfathering route exists. Do not prohibit an otherwise lawful firearm merely because it was acquired abroad.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Secure storage, supervision and transport must prevent unauthorised access. Firearms and ammunition must not be readily accessible together; scrutiny is proportionate to quantity and category.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: For distance purchases, an authorised dealer, broker or authority verifies identity and required authorisation before or on delivery. Applies to category A–C firearms, essential components and ammunition. Includes the Slovenian correction and updated consumer distance-contract definition.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Prohibit acquisition and holding of category A firearms, essential components and ammunition; impound unlawful items.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Optional, individually reasoned security, defence, educational, research and historical exemptions. Collector registers, monitoring and strict security also matter; dealer, broker and museum routes have safeguards. Member States need not adopt every optional relaxation.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: An optional category A6/7 target-shooting authorisation requires medical checks, active competition, twelve months of club training and a qualifying discipline. Includes the limited conscription-related option and review at most every five years.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Optional multi-year acquisition permissions require notification and continuing-condition checks. Possession authorisations are reviewed at most every five years and renewed only while conditions remain satisfied.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Optional grandfathering for formerly category B weapons acquired and registered before 13 June 2017. C234/21 interprets overlapping A9 conversions; it does not annul the directive. Existing 2008 category B holders need no fresh application for their lawfully held C/D weapons, while later transferees must obtain or hold permission.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Category C declaration and transfer notifications include a non-resident’s home Member State. The optional delay for older C5–7 firearms expired on 14 March 2021. Includes the Hungarian reversed-date correction and the 1991 correction covering all relevant C firearms.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Ammunition possession follows equivalent firearm conditions. Large centre-fire magazines require the specified authorisation. Dealers and brokers may refuse suspicious transactions and must report attempts. Includes the Hungarian complete-round correction.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Alarm and signal weapons must be non-convertible; convertible devices count as firearms. Includes the Czech cartridge-chamber correction and chemical-energy scope. Technical standards apply to the specified post-14 September 2018 cohort.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Essential components must be irreversibly disabled, with authority verification, certificate AND mark. Legacy possession is distinguished from placing on the market or transferring. Earlier national standards require the relevant EU equivalence determination, notification and technical fallback.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Distance transfers follow the same procedure. A dealer general authorisation lasts at most three years. The departure Member State receives advance information and may inspect. The exemption list identifies goods that may enter WITHOUT prior consent; English and Swedish corrections do not reverse that meaning.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: EFP travel routes cover hunters and historical re-enactors with C firearms and target shooters with B/C and qualifying A firearms, subject to activity evidence and the specified restrictions. Acceptance cannot carry a fee. Includes Swedish and Danish corrections distinguishing target shooting from competition alone.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Electronic exchange covers transfer authorisations and refusals for security OR reliability. Includes German and Hungarian corrections, national contact details, regular cooperation and destination/transit notifications.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties and enforcement arrangements are required; a standard of mere sufficiency is not equivalent.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Category A includes converted automatic firearms, specified loaded high-capacity centre-fire firearms, functional folding long firearms and acoustic conversions. Includes missile AND launcher, armour-piercing terms, and the lawful hunting OR target-shooting expanding-ammunition exception.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Revised category B capacity, smooth-bore, repeating and semi-automatic distinctions. Capacity is more than three rounds, not at least three. For the at-most-three-round B 5 rule, detachable loading device OR uncertainty that ordinary tools cannot increase capacity: German and Italian 1991 R 01 correct AND to OR; Greek corrects can contain to cannot contain. Historical definitions are followed through 2017 and 2021.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: C5 acoustic conversions, C6 deactivated firearms and C7 single-shot smooth-bore long firearms are included; category D is deleted. Modern reproductions are not exempt merely because they look antique.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: Short firearm means barrel at most thirty centimetres OR overall length at most sixty. Semi-automatic means one shot per trigger operation; repeating includes magazine OR cylinder; automatic means multiple shots per operation. Includes the Finnish, German and Polish corrections and ammunition/projectile definitions.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changeInventory.change: The pass identifies the weapon or firearm, categories, issuer and other Member State authorisations, with updated category A/C travel activities and destination restrictions. Includes the Greek correction.
changeInventory.mandatory: Subject to express Member State options, stronger-protection permission and transitions.

changes.fw-definitions: WaffG Section 1 and Annex 1 include convertible firearms, essential upper/lower receivers, split bolts, ammunition and commercial mediation. Definitions and broader domestic licensing were personally read. Exact treatment of every technical term remains qualified by statutory classification and scope.
changes.fw-residence-pass: Current AWaffV Section 33(1) retains an initial ten-year term for the narrow hunter/sports-shooter single-shot smooth-bore cohort. The original 1991 category D exception was removed by 2008/51 Article 1(1)(e), due 28 July 2010. Some official guidance still gives ten years; other guidance describes five. Published as a qualified document-validity lead after independent adverse review, with no actual issued pass or travel outcome established. Alternative residence proof and full current pass template still require closure.
changes.fw-scope: WaffG Sections 17–18 license collectors and experts; Section 55 retains specified public-service exemptions. The separate current KrWaffKontrG Sections 1–7, 10–13 and 15 were read, including manufacture/transfer permits, entity and director reliability, supervision, records, seizure and state-service exclusions. Full technical classification and all separate-regime transitions remain unclosed.
changes.fw-marks: WaffG Section 24 and AWaffV Section 21 require marking of firearms and essential components, including government-to-civilian transfers, with small-part and historical exceptions. Whole Section 21 was read; the linked technical standards and commencement instruments require final mapping.
changes.fw-dealers-brokers: WaffG Sections 21 and 21a license manufacturing/trade and managers, while Annex 1 Section 2 No 9 includes commercial mediation. Actual official WaffVwV Sections 21.1–21.10 and 21a were read: entity permissions, partner/directing-person reliability checks, register inquiries, foreign applicants and manager permissions. The instruction is from 2012 and does not certify every later administrative practice; no uncovered entity or manager established.
changes.fw-database: Whole current WaffRG Sections 1–34 read, including linked weapon, component, owner and permission data; conversions; updates; access; purpose limits and deletion. Section 27 says deletion at the latest 30 years after destruction, while WaffG Section 44a requires at least 30-year tracing records. Exact combined retention equivalence is legally inconclusive; no early deletion was established.
changes.fw-transaction-registers: WaffG Sections 37–37f require electronic immediate dealer reports and detailed weapon/component data; WaffRG Sections 8–9 route them to the register. Short repair and stock-transfer exceptions use substitute documentation, with AWaffV Sections 17–20 retention/handover. Timeliness and continuous ownership equivalence remain qualified; no untraced weapon established.
changes.fw-licence-age: WaffG Sections 2–4, 10, 12–14 and 27 license ordinary firearms and regulate minimum age, need, suitability and supervised youth hunting/sport. Section 27 was read in full. Exceptions concern limited supervised use; no general underage-purchase exception established.
changes.fw-monitor-withdraw: WaffG Sections 4–6a require periodic reliability/suitability and need checks, medical/psychological evidence and adverse-information reporting; Sections 45–46 require withdrawal and surrender where conditions cease. The discretionary need exception and grandfathered magazines remain expressly qualified.
changes.fw-storage: WaffG Section 36 plus whole AWaffV Section 13 regulate unloaded secure storage, separate or protected ammunition, quantity-sensitive safes and temporary storage. Existing containers, collectors, shared households and individual alternative protection are qualified; actual access and inspections were not audited.
changes.fw-distance: WaffG Sections 34–35 require entitlement and identity checks and expressly address shipping, with transfer permissions under Sections 29–30 preserved. Essential components follow the Annex 1 treatment. No actual remote transaction was examined.
changes.fw-a-prohibition: WaffG Section 2(3), Annex 2 Section 1 and Sections 40–41 prohibit listed weapons and allow seizure. Broader domestic licensing also applies. Separate military-weapons regime and some A-category exceptions remain to close.
changes.fw-a-options: WaffG Sections 17–18 and 40 provide collector/expert and reasoned BKA exception routes with conditions. EU optional derogations do not require a national relaxation. Equivalence of any granted individual permission was not assessed.
changes.fw-a-target: WaffG Section 14 contains age, active club membership and discipline conditions; Section 40 and Annex 2 preserve prohibition and exceptions. Whether an optional A6/7 individual route is used and satisfies every EU condition requires companion-rule confirmation.
changes.fw-periodic: WaffG Section 4(3) requires reliability/suitability review at most every three years and Section 4(4) checks continuing need every five years. Section 10 indefinite possession documents therefore do not alone establish missing review.

changes.eq-definitions: AWGB 1, WGBH/CZ 1 and WGBL 1 use hypothetical comparator and particular-disadvantage definitions; AWGB 1 sexual orientation; AWGB 5/6, WGBH/CZ 4–5 a, WGBL 3–6 employment/vocational training. Operative current bodies read.
changes.eq-access-promotion: All three laws expressly include promotion and training in employment scope: AWGB 5(1) f/g, WGBH/CZ 4 f/g, WGBL 3 f/g. EU duplicated phrase correction does not remove promotion.
changes.eq-accommodation: WGBH/CZ 2 requires effective adjustments according to need unless disproportionate burden;3(1) b/c protective facilities and proportionate positive action. Duty is not limited to premises, and applies to employment/training routes. Actual delivery of adjustments not audited.
changes.eq-occupational: AWGB 5(3) private-relationship exception requires characteristic tied to specific activity/context, genuine/determining job requirement, legitimate aim and proportionate requirement. No obligation to adopt every optional exception; narrower national protection is not a gap.
changes.eq-religious: AWGB 5(2) requires activity/context-linked genuine/legitimate/justified religious occupational requirement, and expressly good faith AND loyalty; cannot entail another prohibited ground, subject indirect-justification rule. AWGB 3 church-internal/spiritual-office exclusion raises classification questions, not established blanket employment nonconformity.
changes.eq-pensions: WGBL 8 optional exception is confined to occupational pension provisions and admission/pension-entitlement ages; it does not exempt all workplace benefits. Exact pension-benefit classification and sex safeguards under other law remain interpretive; optional exception not certified in every application.
changes.eq-age-positive: WGBL 7(1) c requires legitimate objective and appropriate/necessary means;7 a statutory employment-policy and 7 b pension-age retirement are legislated categories, not presumed automatically invalid. WGBH/CZ 3 proportional disability positive measures; EU 7 other positive action optional.
changes.eq-admin-provisions: All three laws expressly reach appointment/dismissal of public officials (AWGB 5(1) d, WGBH/CZ 4 c, WGBL 3 d). Constitution 1 prohibits discrimination;94 disapplies conflicting directly binding treaty/organization rules. Actual abolition of every historical contrary administrative instrument is not established; Constitution 120 limits constitutional review of primary laws and is not treated as a substitute repeal certificate.
changes.eq-remedies: AWGB 9, WGBH/CZ 11, WGBL 13 declare contrary terms void; public-law assistance/representation Awb 2:1/8:24 and associations Awb 1:2(3), private collective BW 3:305 a with statutory safeguards. Termination routes and anti-retaliation in each equality law remain available after the relationship ends; mandatory civil procedural representation rules not exhaustively tested. Current Civil Procedure 79–80 personally read: kanton self-litigation and authorised assistance; advocate rule elsewhere is distinguished from association standing.
